equation_request.abstract:
We discuss decoherence in discrete-time quantum walks in terms of a phenomenological model that distinguishes spin and spatial decoherence. We identify the dominating mechanisms that affect quantum walk experiments realized with neutral atoms walking in an optical lattice.

From the measured spatial distributions, we determine with good precision the amount of decoherence per step, which provides a quantitative indication of the quality of our quantum walks. In particular, we find that spin decoherence is the main mechanism responsible for the loss of coherence in our experiment. We also find that the sole observation of ballistic instead of diffusive expansion in position space is not a good indicator for the range of coherent delocalization.

We provide further physical insight by distinguishing the effects of short and long time spin dephasing mechanisms. We introduce the concept of coherence length in the discrete-time quantum walk, which quantifies the range of spatial coherences. Unexpectedly, we find that quasi-stationary dephasing does not modify the local properties of the quantum walk, but instead affects spatial coherences.

For a visual representation of decoherence phenomena in phase space, we have developed a formalism based on a discrete analogue of the Wigner function. We show that the effects of spin and spatial decoherence differ dramatically in momentum space.

specification.problem: Phenomenological modelling of spin and spatial decoherence in a 1D discrete-time quantum walk (neutral atoms in an optical lattice), with decoherence per step inferred from position distributions.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: a 1D Hadamard-coin discrete-time quantum walk with a generic per-step spin dephasing channel (probability p) and spatial dephasing channel (probability q) acting on the density matrix. Excluded: the paper's specific decoherence model, fitting procedure, quasi-stationary vs. short-time dephasing distinctions, coherence length definition, discrete Wigner function formalism, and experimental parameters.

symbols.meaning: density matrix of walker after t steps
symbols.domain: positive semidefinite, trace 1, on H_spin ⊗ H_pos

equations.label: Unitary step
equations.description: Standard coin-then-shift discrete-time quantum walk step with an assumed Hadamard coin.
equations.justification: Textbook definition of a discrete-time quantum walk; the abstract does not give the coin or shift.

equations.label: Spin dephasing channel
equations.description: Phenomenological spin dephasing applied each step with probability p.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions a phenomenological spin-decoherence model but not its form; the phase-flip channel is a proposed stand-in.
assumptions: Phase-flip (σ_z) channel is a stand-in for the paper's model

equations.label: Spatial dephasing channel
equations.description: Phenomenological spatial dephasing, which damps coherences between neighbouring sites.
equations.justification: The abstract distinguishes spatial decoherence but does not specify its form; this is a proposed simple instance.
assumptions: Parity-dependent phase flip as a stand-in for spatial decoherence

equations.label: Decohered evolution
equations.description: One step of the walk with decoherence after the unitary.
equations.justification: Combines the unitary step and the assumed channels; ordering is a choice.
assumptions: Same p, q at every step

equations.label: Position distribution
equations.description: Measured spatial distribution, from which decoherence per step would be determined by fitting p and q.
equations.abstract_quote: From the measured spatial distributions, we determine with good precision the amount of decoherence per step
equations.justification: The abstract says the decoherence per step is determined from the measured spatial distributions; this is the observable such a fit would use.
assumptions: Spin is traced out in the position measurement

registers.name: position
registers.size: unknown (symbolic, ~log2 of the number of lattice sites)

steps.description: Prepare the walker at the origin with a fixed spin state.
Apply the unitary coin and shift step.
Apply the spin and spatial dephasing channels.
Repeat for t steps, then read out the position distribution.

specification.measurement: Position-resolved measurement (spin traced out), giving P_t(x).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Fit p and q to the measured P_t(x). The fitting method is not specified in the abstract.
assumptions: No experiment scope was given, so a minimal Hadamard walk with phase-flip channels was chosen.
The channel forms and parameters are illustrative, not the paper's.
missing_information: The paper's actual decoherence model and parameters
Definitions of coherence length and the discrete Wigner function
Distinction between short- and long-time (quasi-stationary) dephasing
Experimental coin and shift implementation and initial state
Fitting procedure for decoherence per step
